div.head: II Cn 15.1
div.ab: And se ðe unlage rære oððe undom gedeme heonan forð, for læððe oððe for feohfange, beo se wið þone cingc CXX scyll' scyldig on Engla lage, butan he mid aðe cyðan durre, þæt he hit na rihtor ne cuþe, ⁊ þolige aa his þegnscipes, butan he hine æt þam cingce eft gebicge, swa he him geþafian wylle.

And se ðe unlage ræra oððe undom gedeme heonon forð, for læðþe oððe feohfangce, beo se wið þonne cyningce his weores scyldig on Engla lage, buton he mid aðe cyðan durre, þæt he hit nan rihtor ne cuðe, ⁊ þolige á his ðegenscypes, buton he hine æt þam cyninge gebicge, swa he hym þafian wylle.
And se ðe unlaga arære óððe undom deme heonan forð, for læððe oððe feohfange, beo se wið þone cyngc CXX scill' scildig, . . . buton he geladige, þæt he na bet ne cuðe.

Si quis ammodo (deinceps) únlagam (id est non legem) erigat uel iniustum iudicium iudicet, pro lesione uel aliqua pecunię susceptione, sit erga regem CXX solid. reus in Anglorum laga (lege), nisi cum iuramento audeat inueritare, quod hoc rectius nesciuit, et dignitatem suam legalitatis semper amiserit, nisi (si non) eam redimat erga regem, sicut ei permittet.

⁊ se ðe unlage rǽre oððe undóm gedeme héonan forð, for læððe oððe for feohfange, beo se wið ðone cyng hundtwelftig scill' scyldig on Engla láge, buton he míd aðe cyðan durre, þæt he hit na rihtor ne cuðe, ⁊ ðolie áá his þegenscipes, butan he híne æt ðam cýng gebycge, swa he him geðafian wylle.

And se ðe unlage rære oððe undom gedeme heonon forð, for læððe oððe for feohfange, beo se wið þone cingc CXX scyllinga scyldig on Engla lage—butan he mid aðe cyðan durre, þæt he hit na rihtor ne cuþe—and þolige aa his þegnscipes, butan he hine æt þam cingce eft gebicge, swa he him geþafian wylle. And on Dena lage lahslites scyldig, butan he geladige þæt he na bet ne cuðe.

And he who henceforth promotes injustice or pronounces unjust judgments, as the result of malice or bribery, shall forfeit 120 shillings to the king, in districts under English law, unless he is prepared to declare on oath that he did not know how to give a more just verdict, and he shall lose for ever his rank as a thegn, unless he redeem it from the king, provided the latter is willing to allow him to do so.

And anyone henceforth who promotes injustice or hands down unjust judgments, either because of bias or bribery, shall be liable to the king for one hundred twenty shillings in areas under English law—unless he can declare under oath that he did not know how to deliver a more just sentence—and he shall forfeit forever his rights as a thane, unless he redeems it from the king if he is willing to permit it. In the Danelaw, he shall be liable for his lahslit, unless he can exonerate himself by proving that he did not know any better.

And he who promotes an abuse or gives a wrong judgment henceforth, owing to hatred or bribery, is then to forfeit 120 shillings to the king in the area under English law, unless he dare declare on oath that he knew not how to do it more justly; and he is always to forfeit his thegnly status, unless he may redeem it from the king, according as he will allow him.

Und wer hinfort falsche Satzung (-gen D?) aufstellt oder falsch Urtheil ertheilt aus Hass oder für (fehlt A D) Geldempfang, der sei nach Engländer-Recht gegenüber dem König 120 Schill. (sein Wergeld A) schuldig — ausser wenn er durch Eid zu erweisen wagt, dass er es nicht richtiger wusste — und verliere immer seine Thegnwürde [sammt Gerichtshoheit], ausser wenn er sie (wieder G) vom König auslöst, so wie dieser ihm zu gestatten geruht.

And whoever henceforth sets up an unjust law (laws, D?) or gives a false judgment out of hatred or for (lacking in A D) a bribe, let him be liable to the king for 120 shillings (his wergild, A) under English law — unless he dares to declare on oath that he did not know how to do it more justly — and lose his thegnly rank [with his jurisdiction] for ever, unless he buys it back (again, G) from the king, as the king is willing to permit him.
div.note: D (after VI Atr 40.1) has 15.1–15.3 in a shortened form, missing six lines. G's ‘eft’ is G's addition, as in III Eg 3. Liebermann compares III Eg 3.
This is largely based on III Edgar 3. The Harley MS. has the significant difference that the penalty has arisen from 120 shillings to the delinquent’s wergild.
